From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ruth Delgado <acme-pm@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: Integration blockers & ops asks for product launch window

Team —

Quick note ahead of our QBR prep session: Acme has confirmed the target launch window for the pilot is May 10–14. They expect a canary and full rollout cadence within that week. I ran the most recent integration health check with CS and we now have three categories of risk to surface: ingestion stability (SFTP jobs), model serialization / quantization variance, and regional GPU capacity (us-west burst) that could push latency over our SLO.

I'd like a concise one-pager for the exec pack that captures:
- Current launch timeline and any rebaseline (ask: Lauren)
- Top 5 delivery risks with owner and mitigation ETA (ask: Marcus / Aditya)
- Any ask that needs exec escalation (e.g., extra Dedicated capacity, SLA exception)

Please reply with updates by EOD Monday so I can fold into the QBR deck. I'm looping in Ruth (Acme PM) for visibility; Samir from CloudOps is working on the SFTP resilience fixes and will be an external partner on the mitigation work.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ruth Delgado <acme-pm@acme.com>, Samir Patel <vendor-eng@cloudops.io>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: Integration blockers & ops asks for product launch window

Evelyn —

Thanks for the flag. Short summary from engineering:

1) Ingestion (SFTP): intermittent failures traced to clock skew and retry backpressure on the vendor appliance. Samir's team has a patch in staging that reduces failed transfers by ~60% in our tests; need a production deploy and a canary window. Owner: Samir (vendor) / Marcus (eng). ETA for production patch: 48 hours after sign-off.

2) Model serialization & quantization variance: our 8-bit quantized variant shows a 3.5% drop vs fp16 on a small eval set for one prompt family (document summarization). We can gate quantized model for the pilot and serve fp16 for canary; long-term fix is quantization-aware calibration scheduled next sprint. Owner: Aditya. Mitigation ETA: 2 weeks for calibration; immediate gate for canary.

3) GPU capacity: our us-west pool has a scheduled maintenance on May 11 (cloud provider) that may reduce burst capacity. We can request temporary Dedicated cushion for week of May 10–17 or shift canary earlier. Owner: Marcus / Infrastructure. ETA for capacity approval: 24–72 hours if we raise through sales ops.

I've attached an integration blockers log and a rebaseline timeline (draft). I'm marking two actionable asks for exec consideration:
- Short-term Dedicated capacity bump for May 10–17 (cost + SLA implications)
- Approval to serve fp16 in canary to avoid quality regressions for Acme (this trades cost for quality).

I'll add a concise risk table for the QBR deck and send by EOD Monday.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Engineering
Redwood Inference
